statements.label: Timing
statements.text: April-June across range; late Feb-Mar in Gulf/SE Louisiana; May-early June in Vermont.

statements.label: Temperature
statements.text: 58-66 F; peak about 63 F; 16-19 C (60-66 F) widely repeated; single Alabama milt observation at 14 C (58 F); southern spawn starts Feb.

statements.label: Habitat
statements.text: Shallow weedy water, circular nest 18-30 in across cleared in vegetation/roots near stumps, logs, flooded grass over mud; eggs adhesive; male guards nest and fry.

statements.label: Shallow movement
statements.text: Adults move shallow during breeding season, spawning mostly at night.

statements.label: Pre-spawn
statements.text: Fish move toward large marshy/vegetated embayments (Oneida Lake telemetry); southern fish start Feb-Mar.

statements.label: Post-spawn
statements.text: Females and larger fish disperse several km (5-20 km northern); males stay with fry to ~4 in.

statements.label: What triggers movement
statements.text: Spawn onset around 16-19 C; air-breathing rate rises above ~10 C and peaks ~18-30 C (65-85 F).

statements.label: Pre-spawn
statements.text: Staging in marshy embayments as water nears upper 50s F.

statements.label: Spawn
statements.text: 60-66 F, nocturnal.

statements.label: Summer
statements.text: Tolerates very warm, low-oxygen water; uses warm stable shallows.

statements.label: Cold-water slowdown
statements.text: Below ~10 C air breathing and activity decline; fish hold in sheltered warm vegetated spots.

statements.label: Shallow when
statements.text: Spawn season; night; warm vegetated embayments (<~2.3 m, many sites 1.3-2.7 m).

statements.label: Deeper when
statements.text: Daytime in some accounts (adults mostly in deeper water); winter inner harbour use was low in Toronto.

statements.label: Useful depth and habitat
statements.text: Shallow vegetated cover under ~2 m; nest water depth likely about 1-2 ft (low confidence).

statements.label: Rising water
statements.text: Likely uses newly flooded vegetation and floodplain (inferred; Louisiana early spawn coincides with high water).

statements.label: Falling water
statements.text: Can bury in mud and survive weeks in drying habitat; fish stranded on floodplains reported.

statements.label: Flooded shoreline
statements.text: Nests in flooded grasses over mud near shore.

statements.label: Current
statements.text: Still to slow water; avoids current.

statements.label: River discharge
statements.text: No data.

statements.label: Backwater connection
statements.text: Floodplain/backwater/oxbow use well described; connectivity matters (inferred).

statements.label: vegetationAssociation
statements.text: Strongest driver: residency increased with percent submerged vegetation (p<0.001, Toronto); nests built in dense vegetation and root mats.

statements.label: coverAndSubstrate
statements.text: Stumps, logs, undercut banks, submerged branches, root mats; mud or sand/gravel nest bottom.

statements.label: Day
statements.text: Holds in cover, often deeper or in dense weeds.

statements.label: Dusk
statements.text: Feeding begins.

statements.label: Night
statements.text: Primarily nocturnal; moves shallow to feed; spawns mostly at night.

statements.label: Dawn
statements.text: Feeding continues.

statements.label: Bright sun
statements.text: Likely holds in dense cover (inferred).

statements.label: Low light
statements.text: Feeds and moves shallow at dawn, dusk and night.

statements.label: Turbid water
statements.text: Tolerates silt and mud.

statements.label: Clear water
statements.text: Prefers clear vegetated water; clear water makes fish in weeds visible to a light.

statements.label: Main river
statements.text: Backwater/eddy margins only.

statements.label: Reservoir
statements.text: Vegetated coves and embayments.

statements.label: Creek / tributary
statements.text: Slow lowland creek reaches with weed.

statements.label: Backwater / slough
statements.text: Core habitat: sloughs, oxbows, swamps.

statements.label: Shoreline / flat
statements.text: Weedy flats at night and spawn.

statements.label: Channel edge
statements.text: Weed edges at sandbars and channel margins.

bowfisherGuide.takeaway: A bowfisher looking for bowfin should concentrate on shallow, weedy, still backwaters, sloughs and coves at night, especially spring at 58-66 F when males sit on nests near stumps and flooded grass, and watch for surface air gulps in warm low-oxygen weed beds.
